module: Non-Accidental Trauma, Salter-Harris Fractures and Bone Infections
subject: ss-paediatric-radiology
title: Non-Accidental Trauma (NAT): High-Specificity Skeletal Lesions

steps.say: Classic metaphyseal lesions carry the highest specificity for physical abuse in infants. Planar shearing forces from violent shaking fracture the fragile primary spongiosa.
steps.tx: Recognize the **classic metaphyseal lesion specificity** on high-detail skeletal radiographs. Classic metaphyseal lesions (CML), manifesting as corner fractures or bucket-handle fractures, are practically pathognomonic of non-accidental trauma in infants under 2 years of age. They result from violent pulling, twisting, or shaking forces that produce microfractures across the primary spongiosa of the metaphysis parallel to the growth plate (Posterior rib fractures).

left.title: Corner fracture projection
points: X-ray beam tangential to peripheral rim
Involves distal femur or proximal tibia

right.title: Bucket-handle projection
points: X-ray beam angled oblique to growth plate
Crescentic disc-like rim of mineralized bone

steps.say: Posterior rib fractures adjacent to the costovertebral joint are classic for manual squeezing of an infant chest. They are virtually never caused by accidental household falls.
steps.tx: Identify **posterior rib fractures** as definitive indicators of violent thoracic compression. Manual squeezing of an infant chest compresses the anterior thorax against the posterior costovertebral articulation, using the transverse processes of the spine as a fulcrum. These fractures occur near the costovertebral joints and are virtually never produced by cardiopulmonary resuscitation or accidental falls from a bed (Skeletal survey protocol).

rows: Fall with outstretched arm / birth trauma

steps.say: A complete skeletal survey requires at least twenty-one dedicated high-resolution views. Never settle for an abbreviated study or a babygram when child abuse is suspected.
steps.tx: Perform a complete **skeletal survey 21 views** according to ACR and SPR guidelines. An infant suspected of non-accidental trauma requires dedicated, high-detail separate radiographs of every body region, encompassing at least 21 individual views. Babygrams (single whole-body exposures) are unacceptable due to severe geometric distortion and inadequate resolution to detect subtle metaphyseal fractures (Two-week follow-up survey).

rows: AP, lateral, and bilateral oblique ribs
Separate AP views of arms, forearms, hands, thighs, legs, feet

steps.say: A repeat skeletal survey at ten to fourteen days detects occult fractures that were invisible on initial presentation. Subperiosteal healing and callus make healing fractures obvious.
steps.tx: Schedule a mandatory **follow-up skeletal survey at 2 weeks** post-injury. Acute non-displaced fractures and metaphyseal injuries may be radiographically occult on initial emergency presentation. Repeating the skeletal survey after 10-14 days unmasks these fractures because subperiosteal new bone formation, osteopenia, and callus remodeling become prominently visible, establishing the true extent and chronology of injuries (Salter-Harris injuries).

steps.say: The Salter-Harris system categorizes physeal fractures from type one to five. Type two is by far the most frequent, characterized by the triangular Thurston Holland metaphyseal fragment.
steps.tx: Master the **Salter-Harris classification SALTR** for pediatric growth plate injuries. Type I involves slipped physis alone; Type II fractures above the physis through the metaphysis (accounting for 75% of all physeal injuries, featuring the Thurston Holland corner fragment); Type III fractures lower into the epiphysis; Type IV passes through both metaphysis and epiphysis; and Type V represents crush injury of the physis with high risk of growth arrest (Toddler fracture).

rows: Lower into epiphysis into joint space
High risk of physeal bony bridge
Rammed / crush injury of germinal physis

steps.say: A toddler fracture is a benign accidental injury seen when an infant begins to walk. It manifests as a non-displaced spiral fracture of the distal tibia without fibular injury.
steps.tx: Distinguish an accidental **toddler fracture** from non-accidental trauma. A toddler fracture is an isolated, non-displaced, oblique or spiral fracture of the distal third of the tibial shaft in ambulatory children aged 9 months to 3 years. It results from low-energy torsional twisting during normal play, presenting with sudden refusal to bear weight without soft tissue bruising or associated fibular fracture (Acute osteomyelitis).

left.title: Toddler fracture (accidental)
points: Intact fibula with no soft tissue contusion
Low-energy fall in ambulatory 9 mo to 3 yr

steps.say: Magnetic resonance imaging is the most sensitive technique for pediatric osteomyelitis. Low T1 marrow signal and high T2 edema indicate infection days before radiographs show changes.
steps.tx: Rely on **acute osteomyelitis MRI sensitivity** exceeding 95% in pediatric bone infections. Plain radiographs remain normal for the first 10-14 days until 30-50% of bone mineral is lost. MRI demonstrates infection within hours of onset, revealing replacement of normal hyperintense T1 fatty marrow with hypointense inflammatory exudate, hyperintense T2/STIR marrow edema, periosteal elevation, and subperiosteal abscess (Septic arthritis).

rows: Deep soft tissue swelling; late periosteal reaction
Replacement of bright marrow fat with low signal

steps.say: Ultrasound is the imaging modality of choice for suspected septic arthritis of the hip. Capsular distension greater than two millimeters compared to the normal hip warrants urgent needle aspiration.
steps.tx: Perform **septic arthritis ultrasound** for any child presenting with a painful, irritable hip and fever. Longitudinal anterior hip sonography measures the anterior capsular-femoral distance: an effusion measuring > 2 mm thicker than the asymptomatic contralateral side confirms joint pathology. Ultrasound-guided aspiration is mandatory to obtain synovial fluid for gram stain and culture to prevent femoral head avascular necrosis.

nodes.label: Child with fever, hip pain & refusal to bear weight
